title: The CNS behind a barrier
objective: Explain why the CNS relies on resident immune cells behind the blood–brain barrier.

steps.title: A guarded compartment
steps.body: The **[[blood–brain barrier]] (BBB)** tightly limits what crosses from blood into the brain — including most blood-borne immune cells. So the CNS leans on **resident** immune cells, chiefly **[[microglia]]**, to patrol it. This is why CNS immunity looks different from the rest of the body.

steps.prompt: Why does the CNS depend so heavily on resident microglia rather than blood-borne immune cells?
options: The blood–brain barrier limits entry of circulating immune cells
The brain has no lymphatic drainage, so immune cells never reach it
Circulating immune cells cannot survive in cerebrospinal fluid
Microglia are the only cells able to clear debris in any tissue
steps.explanation: The BBB restricts circulating immune cells, so the CNS keeps its own resident sentinels (microglia) on constant patrol.

variants.setup: Circulating immune cells mostly can't cross into the healthy brain.
variants.prompt: How is the CNS still surveilled?
options: By resident microglia already inside it
By antibodies crossing the barrier from the blood
variants.reveal: Resident microglia patrol the CNS from within, since the BBB blocks most blood immune cells.

steps.setup: A severe injury breaks down the blood–brain barrier in one region.
options: Blood-borne immune cells can now enter that region
Only small molecules cross; immune cells still cannot
Microglia there stop surveying while the barrier is open
The barrier reseals before anything can cross into the tissue
steps.reveal: A broken barrier lets circulating immune cells infiltrate — a hallmark of many CNS injuries and diseases, and a reason neuroinflammation can escalate.

variants.prompt: If the BBB breaks down locally, what can happen?
options: Blood immune cells infiltrate the tissue
Only small molecules cross, never cells
Microglia stop surveying while it is open
variants.explanation: A breached barrier allows peripheral immune cells into the CNS.

reviewNotes: BBB + resident immunity; builds on B4 microglia.
